gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-imperial: Vintage muscle from Woodgod, its lowercase nearly reaching the capitals. Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic, a plain sans with pincer-like open c ends, gives it a friendly partner that never competes for attention.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-kharosht: Loud vintage swagger from Woodgod, wide channels cut into every bowl. Noto Sans Kharoshthi, a sans-serif with curves that never close back on themselves and a dark, dense stripe of lowercase, is the sturdy foil.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-khudawad: Big vintage voice, with bowls cut wide. Woodgod does commanding display lettering, while Noto Sans Khudawadi, a plain sans with unsealed rounds, does the quiet, clean job of carrying text.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-old-ital: Vintage punch from Woodgod, lowercase nearly matching its capitals. Noto Sans Old Italic, a plain sans with curve endings kept well apart, should read smoothly down a full page of text.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-syloti-n: Noto Sans Syloti Nagri reads tall and clean, with short ascenders. Beneath Woodgod's commanding, wide-bowled lettering, its open-bowled a lets the text breathe while the heading does the barking.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-numans: Vintage force from Woodgod, wide channels in every bowl. Numans, a plain sans with widely spaced tracking and far-hanging s ends, gives it a modern, clean foil that loosens the heading's weight.
gen-gf-iansui-outfit: Iansui feels hand-drawn, with gently flared curve ends. Outfit, a sans-serif with curves that finish before they close, steps in beside it, and the pair feels friendliest in brief bursts.
gen-gf-mali-fs-recia: Mali leads with casual, inviting handwriting, its c tips held well apart. Recia, a serif of light modulation and generous openings, adds a sharper, authoritative footing, handy for a couple of lines of text.
